body.text: 264 commits landed across 6 repositories this week. The heaviest activity was in gm (234 commits), followed by design (10).
gm -- 234 commits

feat: no-surprise MO - transform memorized workarounds into positive predictable changes (user directive). Principle: we work USING gm, not ON it, so a memorized workaround / known-limitation / internal-advice is tribal knowledge that surprises a fresh user/LLM -- everything must be abundantly predictable at face value, no surprises ever. AGENTS.md Core Rule now codifies the transform discipline: a workaround-memo resolves one of three ways then is pruned -- (a) already in standing prose -> prune; (b) prose-worthy absent -> add to prose + prune; (c) genuine surprising behavior -> fix code + prune; recall carries project work-context, never tool-operation advice. Transforms applied this fire: codesearch cwd-scope -> SKILL.md search rule + gm-plugkit/instructions/entry.md inspection-routing prose clause (the limitation now predictable at face value; the search-reflex advice memo pruned); recurring CRLF/LF const-drift -> .gitattributes eol=lf pin on the prose surfaces (gm + rs-plugkit, ending the autocrlf churn). Memorized the governing principle (the lone recall-worthy meta-rule about recall hygiene).

feat(skill): enforce single-witness test rule in the skillfile + sync LF-normalization. skills/gm-skill/SKILL.md gains the standing guaranteed-read rule 'The test surface is a single real-services integration witness, not a unit suite' (one test.js at root, <=200 lines, real services/mock-free; a growing mock-heavy multi-file test/ directory is the conventional-testing tell-tale gm replaces, never a blessed gate beside the witness; test.js being capped does not exempt a parallel suite; more than the single witness is a re-scope to justify) -- the test discipline was VERIFY-phase-prose-only, so an agent writing tests in EXECUTE never saw it; 'move important rules into the skillfile'. gm-plugkit/instructions/verify.md clarified to match. gm-plugkit/scripts/sync-instruction-consts.mjs strips CRLF so the .md<->.rs consts stop recurringly drifting (the bundle .md is CRLF on Windows, local sync emitted CRLF consts vs CI's LF). Surfaced from a dstate agent rationalizing a 24-file mock unit suite as exempt from the single-file test rule; fixed the RULE so every agent applies it, did not touch foreign dstate's tests.

feat(gate): enforce search-discipline at dispatch (deviation.native-search-bash). The audit-loop workflow caught a search-discipline gate-miss: native grep -r in a gm cwd was only flagged post-hoc by ccsniff, never blocked at dispatch like bash-git-bypass. checkDispatchGates now blocks native tree-search Bash (grep -r/-R/-rl/-rn, --recursive, standalone rg) with a reason naming the codesearch verb, mirroring the spool-poll/bash-git-bypass gates. Conservative detector: pipe-filter (cmd|grep), grep --color, grep -E/-n on a named file, and rg --version all pass (tested 9/9 allow, 7/7 block). Makes the discipline structural - predictable regardless of which LLM drives the harness - not reliant on model compliance.

feat(audit-loop): add supervisor upgrade-resilience health scan. The audit workflow checked cascade/gmsniff/ccsniff/version-source/residual but not supervisor health, despite supervisor.giving-up + version-drift crash-loops being the dominant gm operational defect of the last 3 fires. New 6th parallel Scan agent flags any supervisor stuck in giving-up state or churning version-drift, and verifies the two-layer resilience (restart-burst backoff + version-drift cooldown) is present in the running supervisor.js. Verdict broken on a dead/giving-up supervisor or a missing resilience layer.
